gap_notes: The stored chain keeps 743 zero-bid lines; the zero-bid stop rule is applied as published.

The replication is timed at the book's quote time, 2026-11-11 04:27 ET, as Cboe times a calculation on the quotes standing then; the Cboe close it is compared with is the 16:15 ET print of 2026-11-10, so the gap includes the market's move between the two instants.
Model variance swaps at 30 days (k in [-3, 2], wings beyond the fitted K/F 0.70-1.30 extrapolated, so each inherits its model's wing bias): SVI-cal 18.26, SVI 18.37, eSSVI 17.67.

Gap attribution (VIX, SVI-cal surface): replicated - official = -0.67. Strikes beyond the stored strip would add +0.00 under the surface's wing; the stored quotes beyond the fitted K/F 0.70-1.30 are 0.36 index points richer than that wing, so the truncation figure likely understates. Inside the fitted range market and surface differ by +0.12 (these two terms set the replication against the surface; they are not part of the gap). Left unexplained by the chain: +0.66 (official - replicated - truncation; 99% of official - replicated): snapshot timing vs the 16:15 ET print, stale quotes.

rate.source: The session close's curve: the U.S. Treasury par yield curve (CMT) of 2026-11-09, the newest before the session, the one Cboe computes the session's close with, at Cboe's tenors. Each term's rate is Cboe's bounded natural cubic spline at its expiration, in calendar days counted from that curve's date as Cboe's published sample counts them, the bond-equivalent yield taken to an annual percentage yield and then to continuous compounding (Cboe Volatility Index Mathematics Methodology sec. 2.1). A book timed after the close (in Global Trading Hours) keeps this curve and this day count, so each term's rate is the one the Cboe close it is compared with used; each term records the rate it used
